tables.model_routing_hint: Use this table when the user asks about subassembly lots linked to work orders, serial-numbered subcomponents, quantity balances, or status tracking of subassemblies. Use PRD_M_WORK_ORDER for work order header data and PRD_M_ITEM for item master data.

tables.business_purpose: Captures the execution timeline and quantitative outcomes of work orders on the shop floor, including produced quantities, quality status breakdowns, and temporal tracking of production activities. This table logs the actual progress of work orders rather than storing master data, making it essential for real-time production monitoring and variance analysis between planned vs actual outputs.
tables.row_represents: One execution instance of a work order, recording production quantities, quality status, timestamps, and linkage to sales orders or customer requirements.
use_when: Tracking production progress against planned quantities
Analyzing quality breakdowns (accepted/rejected/scrap)
Finding work order execution start/end dates
Checking in-progress or hold quantities on a job
Linking work orders to sales orders or customer POs
Auditing production execution history
Comparing total vs produced quantities
Identifying work orders with incomplete data
Finding work order status changes over time
Analyzing production performance by date range
